newsitem.title: USA: ATTACK ON AMERICA'S CUP TROPHY CONDEMNED.
newsitem.headline: ATTACK ON AMERICA'S CUP TROPHY CONDEMNED.

text.p: New York Yacht Club Vice Commodore George Isdale on Thursday condemned the attack on the America's Cup trophy as a senseless act of violence and said the values it represented would remain untarnished.
A man wielding a sledgehammer and shouting Maori slogans badly damaged the Auld Mug, the yachting trophy that Team New Zealand won in 1995.
The man, who has been arrested, walked into the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron in Auckland, pulled out a sledgehammer and began striking the glass case in which the cup is housed.
Isdale said he was shocked and saddened to learn of the attack which badly damaged the trophy.

"We are sure the people of New Zealand are as distressed as we are about this senseless act of violence," he said in a written statement. "Despite any physical damage to the cup, we know that the values and traditions it represents will never be tarnished."
No estimate of the damage was immediately available, but the cup was insured for US$2 million when it was held by the San Diego Yacht Club.
Isdale said the America's Cup was the oldest trophy in competitive sport and one that sailors from the New York Yacht Club had defended for 132 years.
